characterList.description: We don't see this person, but we hear them narrating.
characterList.name: Narrator

content_metadata.description: A video presentation demonstrating how diffraction gratings can separate white light into its component colors and how our visual system perceives color.

qAndA.answer: The program cycles a bar through different colors to demonstrate how color is perceived by the human eye.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the program shown on the screen?

qAndA.answer: The narrator is sliding a diffraction grating onto the screen.
qAndA.question: What is the narrator sliding onto the screen?

qAndA.answer: The white bar appears as separate red, green, and blue bars due to the diffraction grating separating the white light.
qAndA.question: What happens to the white bar when the diffraction grating is applied?

qAndA.answer: The bottom bar appears to change color, but in reality, it's just red, green, and blue light fading in and out at different intensities.
qAndA.question: What happens to the bottom bar as it cycles through different colors?

qAndA.answer: The narrator is demonstrating that the colors we perceive are created by our visual system processing different combinations of red, green, and blue light.
qAndA.question: What is the main point the narrator is making?

text_to_speech: here's a little test program it's just cycling that bottom bar through every color I'm going to slide in a diffraction grating and you can see the white on the top is actually just red green and blue and on the bottom as it cycles through all the other colors it's just fading in red green and blue a different intensities and all the actual colors you see are just an artifact of your own visual system

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Here's a little test program. It's just cycling that bottom bar through every color.
I'm going to slide in at a fraction grading.
And you can see that white on the top is actually just red, green, and blue.
And on the bottom as it cycles through all the other colors, it's just fading in red, green, and blue at different intensities.
And all the actual colors you see are just an artifact of your own visual system.
